book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Current fee for what a solicitor does?

parts.note: a fee is the cost of a service

explanation.surface: A query about the charge a lawyer makes for their services.
explanation.walkthrough: The solicitor is not a lawyer but someone soliciting in the street, who approaches passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching strangers boldly with an offer is exactly what a street prostitute does when soliciting custom.

clue.text: Disease said to be upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting knocks over, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A distressing illness, or so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' looks like a sound signal, but it is simply the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: AIDS is the syndrome caused by HIV, an illness that attacks the immune system.

clue.text: Dubious act featuring nude entertainment

indicators.note: featuring means holding inside, so the second word is enclosed
something dubious is not quite right, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A questionable strip show passed off as a night's amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is the entertainment of songs, comedy and dance staged in a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: Row not unusual in Irish political arena

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Quarrels are routine in Northern Ireland's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormont is the Belfast estate housing Northern Ireland's parliament, so it stands for that region's politics.

clue.text: Endless old king and queen could raise a strain

definitions.note: the clue's verb points to the kitchen strainer

indicators.note: without its end, the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A tale of royalty whose music might strike up a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the 'merry old soul' of the nursery rhyme; a strain is also a snatch of music, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is the perforated kitchen bowl used to strain vegetables or pasta, draining off water.

clue.text: Upright youth first takes lid off public misconduct

indicators.note: first says which phrase leads, so the lid-lifting phrase goes before the boy

parts.note: one who takes the lid off opens a can

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing upright means the word is written from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A decent young man lifting the lid on a public outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' looks like praise for the youth's honesty, but it reverses LAD in this down entry. The phrase for taking a lid off is read as OPENS CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An open scandal is a disgraceful affair that everyone knows about, wrongdoing out in public view.

clue.text: Come down in flames

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to descend, as from a vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a crashing aircraft; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to step off a bus or land, while the adjective means on fire.

clue.text: Nonconformist gets a kick …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who rejects conventional society
second meaning: in rugby, a restart kick from the 22-metre line

explanation.surface: A rebel finding a thrill, with the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union a drop-out is the drop kick that restarts play from the defending side's 22.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropout abandons conventional life or study, and the rugby restart is likewise named.

clue.text: … from church teaching and activity linked with good conduct

definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it: the cut in sentence earned by good conduct

parts.note: a church's mission, its evangelising work

explanation.surface: Continuing 7: a thrill gained from religious instruction and good works.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners may earn time off their sentence for behaving well in jail, which is that kind of early release.

clue.text: Borrower begins to be in the red — just about

parts.words: begins to be in the red
parts.note: surface: someone whose bank account is starting to slip into overdraft
setter's reading: a borrower is pretty much by definition one who owes money

explanation.surface: A borrower whose account is starting to dip below zero.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in the red' means owing money, which is what a person who has borrowed does.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who has taken a loan owes money to the lender, making them a party owing a sum.

clue.text: Nothing barred in bedroom drama in Spain

definitions.note: the answer is a resort in Spain, not the country

indicators.note: a drama is a commotion, so the letters are thrown about
something barred is shut out, so the nought is kept out of the room word

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
the first in, taken as written

explanation.surface: Anything goes in a steamy bedroom scene set on the Spanish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one O from BEDROOM, add IN, and rearrange to get BENIDORM, the package-holiday resort on Spain's Costa Blanca.
explanation.definitionFit: Benidorm is a famous seaside holiday resort on the Costa Blanca, so it is a place found in that country.

clue.text: Where girls start stirring up classroom, harm can result…

definitions.text: Where girls start stirring up classroom, harm can result

indicators.note: stirring things up mixes them, so the letters are jumbled together
the start of the word girls means only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Trouble breaking out when girls start causing a commotion in class.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a wry description of selective schools; the ellipsis carries on into 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar schools are the selective secondary schools where pupils, girls included, start and where classroom mischief may occur.

clue.text: Steal the picture?

parts.note: to abstract is to take away, a formal word for stealing
a picture is a work of art

explanation.walkthrough: 'Abstract' as a verb means to remove or pinch, so the whole clue is both the instruction and a playful definition of a style of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract art is non-representational painting of shapes and colours, and the clue reads it as an order to pinch some.

clue.text: one enters college with indecent haste — one does when jiggered

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one is placed within the school name

parts.note: Eton College, the English public school

indicators.note: indecent suggests something improper, out of its right order

explanation.surface: Someone rushing into college unseemly fast, carrying on from the schools clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The lowercase opening continues the ellipsis from 11 across. 'I'll be jiggered!' and 'I'll eat my hat!' are both British exclamations of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly astonished might exclaim they will consume their headgear, the same surprise as being jiggered.

clue.text: Admit it's a matter of gut reaction

parts.note: to admit is to let enter

explanation.surface: Confessing that a decision was purely instinctive.
explanation.walkthrough: A gut reaction is normally an instinct; here it is a literal reaction in the intestines.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis is inflammation of the intestine, so the bowel is literally reacting badly.

clue.text: Small case with free tuition thrown in

indicators.note: what is thrown in is included inside the phrase, so the letters sit within it

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A little bag that comes with lessons included at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles, scissors or cosmetics, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Flatter and rather mild?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to coax with compliments
second meaning: read as bland plus the suffix -ish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a comparative of flat, joined to mildness as if describing a landscape or a taste.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to cajole with sweet talk, and split as bland-ish it means somewhat insipid.

clue.text: Difficulty of model question

explanation.surface: A problem with a sample exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Ford's famous early car, so model gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A task can mean an onerous piece of work, a burdensome job, close to a difficulty or challenge.

clue.text: Cruel as humanism may be?

definitions.note: adjective phrase describing what humanism is

indicators.note: may be hints the letters could take another form if rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe that a godless worldview is heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanism rests on human reason rather than religion, so it is non-religious in outlook.

clue.text: One glad to go about in brown dress

indicators.note: in places the combined letters inside the colour word
going about means turning around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A happy person walking about in a brown frock.
explanation.walkthrough: The one and the jumbled word are combined first, and that group is then placed inside the colour after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridal gown is the dress a bride wears at her wedding, a specific kind of dress.

clue.text: Nothing to share but words

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone offers only talk, nothing tangible.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, so it is made of spoken words delivered at length.

clue.text: Altogether lacking in harmony?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in 'in ...', all at once
second meaning: singing the same note, with no chordal parts

explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies discord, but voices in unison share a single line, so there is no harmony at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together all at once is doing so in concert, and musically a single shared pitch carries no chords.

clue.text: Evidence that time flies, of course

definitions.text: Evidence that time flies, of course

parts.note: surface: proof of how fast time passes, like a calendar on the wall
setter's reading: a calendar for the racecourse, listing when horses fly round the track

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' seems to mean 'naturally' but points to the racecourse; a fixture list tells you when the horses will fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing calendar is the published schedule of race meetings, a record of dates on the turf.

clue.text: Disposition of men and women vying with one another?

indicators.note: the letters come from two words held with one another, straddling the gap

parts.note: across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: The temperament of the sexes competing against each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Rivals vying with one another are often driven by this very feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is a resentful frame of mind toward another's luck, a state of feeling or temperament.

clue.text: Latin mass curtailed and turned into pagan symbol

indicators.note: turned into implies a transformation, a change of letter order
curtailed means its tail is cut, losing the last letter

explanation.surface: A church service shortened and converted into heathen ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object believed to have magic powers, a charm of the kind found in pre-Christian belief.

clue.text: Car takes on pet

indicators.note: the car takes the next word along with it, placed after

parts.note: the Mini, a small British car

explanation.surface: A vehicle giving a lift to an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is the classic small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion was originally a favourite or darling, a person treated like a pet by a patron.

clue.text: Romantic music for an Easter service

indicators.note: a service puts things to work, rearranging them for new use

explanation.surface: Love songs to be played at a church celebration in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenata is an evening serenade or cantata, a piece of music suited to wooing a beloved.

clue.text: Pooh starts on his little something false

indicators.note: how the bear's name starts, that is, only its opening letter

parts.note: the initial of the bear's name
Winnie-the-Pooh's 'little something' is always a pot of honey

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh setting off on his snack, with something fishy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: In A. A. Milne's stories Pooh is forever wanting 'a little something', meaning honey.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney describes something fake, counterfeit or insincere, a synonym for not genuine.
